question: Given \(\angle 1+\angle 2=180^\circ\), \(\angle 2+\angle 3=180^\circ\), \(\angle 1=2x+10^\circ\), and \(\angle 3=3x-20^\circ\), find the value of \(x\).
solution: Supplements of the same angle are equal, so \(\angle 1=\angle 3\). Thus \(2x+10=3x-20\), which gives \(x=30\).

Method 1: Equate the two supplements

Supplements of the same angle are equal, so \(\angle 1=\angle 3\). Thus \(2x+10=3x-20\), which gives \(x=30\).
